original_question: Can one explore a version of the McKay correspondence over global fields, especially number fields?
target_in_paper: Section 13, Problem 13.1: "Explore the McKay correspondence over global fields, in particular, number fields." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it correctly targets the global-field version of the McKay correspondence, keeps number fields as the emphasized case, and preserves the paper’s intentionally exploratory wording rather than turning it into a stronger theorem claim. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
missing_details: The paper means a global analogue of the local wild McKay correspondence in stringy-motive form, specifically the local identity (2.6), not just an unspecified "version" of the correspondence. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The local model being globalized compares a geometric quantity on the quotient variety with an arithmetic quantity built from G-torsors over the punctured formal disk; that geometry/arithmetic template is part of the intended meaning. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

For number fields, the paper explicitly points to the interplay between the Batyrev-Manin conjecture and the Malle conjecture as the prime candidate framework for the global theory. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The two counting problems singled out are: rational points of bounded height on the geometric side, and Galois extensions with bounded discriminant on the arithmetic side. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The nearby discussion indicates that one should compare not only the existence of two counting theories, but also their asymptotic exponents and constants. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The paper highlights specific structural matches behind those asymptotics: index versus discrepancy, the number of K-conjugacy classes of minimal index versus the number of crepant divisors, and Bhargava/Peyre-type leading constants. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The scope is global fields in general, with number fields as the main emphasized special case; the draft only hints at this but does not state it outright. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
refined_question: For a global field K, especially a number field, can one formulate and develop a global analogue of the local stringy-motive McKay correspondence (2.6) for quotient varieties attached to finite group actions, in which the geometric counting problem of K-rational points of bounded height on the relevant quotient/Fano-type variety is related to the arithmetic counting problem of Galois extensions of K with bounded discriminant, in a way compatible with the Batyrev-Manin and Malle conjectures, including their predicted exponents and leading constants? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
justification: The draft clearly points to Section 13 rather than to any earlier problem: its wording is essentially that of Problem 13.1 itself. The surrounding text then explains what the author means by this problem—namely, a global counterpart to the local wild McKay correspondence (2.6), with number fields emphasized because the expected bridge should relate the Batyrev-Manin conjecture on rational points and the Malle conjecture on field extensions. Sharpening the draft by naming those two sides and the asymptotic data they should match makes the question stand-alone and paper-faithful without narrowing it to the more specific follow-up Problems 13.2 or 13.3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
